source.title: More Control Flow Tools
source.label: Tutorial Python · Pengatur Aliran Program (Control Flow)

blocks.html: Pernyataan if
Mungkin jenis pernyataan yang paling dikenal luas adalah pernyataan if. Sebagai contoh:

>>> x = int(input("Please enter an integer: ")) Please enter an integer: 42 >>> if x < 0: ... x = 0 ... print('Negative changed to zero') ... elif x == 0: ... print('Zero') ... elif x == 1: ... print('Single') ... else: ... print('More') ... More
blocks.text:
>>> x = int(input("Please enter an integer: "))
Please enter an integer: 42
>>> if x < 0:
...     x = 0
...     print('Negative changed to zero')
... elif x == 0:
...     print('Zero')
... elif x == 1:
...     print('Single')
... else:
...     print('More')
...
More

blocks.html: Dapat terdapat nol atau lebih bagian elif, dan bagian else bersifat opsional. Kata kunci 'elif' merupakan singkatan dari 'else if', dan berguna untuk menghindari indentasi berlebih. Rangkaian if … elif … elif … bertindak sebagai pengganti pernyataan switch atau case yang ada di bahasa lain.

Jika Anda membandingkan nilai yang sama dengan beberapa konstanta atau memeriksa tipe data tertentu, pernyataan match juga dapat digunakan. Rincian selengkapnya dapat dilihat pada dokumentasi match statements.
Pernyataan pass
Pernyataan pass tidak melakukan tindakan apa pun. Pernyataan ini digunakan saat suatu pernyataan dibutuhkan secara sintaksis tetapi program tidak memerlukan aksi apa pun. Sebagai contoh:
>>> while True: ... pass # Busy-wait for keyboard interrupt (Ctrl+C) ...
blocks.text:
>>> while True:
...     pass  # Busy-wait for keyboard interrupt (Ctrl+C)
...

blocks.html: Pernyataan ini umumnya digunakan untuk membuat kerangka kelas minimal:
>>> class MyEmptyClass: ... pass ...

Tempat lain penggunaan pass adalah sebagai penampung sementara (place-holder) untuk badan fungsi atau blok percabangan saat Anda merancang kode baru, memungkinkan Anda berpikir pada level abstraksi yang lebih tinggi tanpa memicu SyntaxError:
>>> def initlog(*args): ... pass # Remember to implement this! ...
blocks.text:
>>> def initlog(*args):
...     pass   # Remember to implement this!
...

source.title: Compound statements
source.label: Referensi Bahasa Python · Pernyataan Majemuk (Compound Statements)

blocks.html: Pernyataan if
Pernyataan if digunakan untuk eksekusi kode kondisional berdasarkan pemenuhan syarat tertentu:
if_stmt ::= "if" assignment_expression ":" suite ("elif" assignment_expression ":" suite)* ["else" ":" suite]
blocks.text:
if_stmt ::= "if" assignment_expression ":" suite
            ("elif" assignment_expression ":" suite)*
            ["else" ":" suite]

blocks.html: Pernyataan ini memilih tepat satu blok kode (suite) dengan mengevaluasi ekspresi kondisi satu per satu hingga ditemukan kondisi yang bernilai benar (True). Blok kode tersebut kemudian dieksekusi. Jika seluruh ekspresi bernilai salah (False), blok klausa else (jika ada) yang akan dijalankan.

source.title: Expressions
source.label: Referensi Bahasa Python · Perbandingan & Operasi Boolean

blocks.html: Perbandingan (Comparisons)

Berbeda dengan bahasa C, semua operasi perbandingan di Python memiliki prioritas yang sama, yaitu lebih rendah daripada operasi aritmetika dan pergeseran bit. Selain itu, ekspresi seperti a < b < c memiliki interpretasi berantai seperti dalam matematika formal:
comparison ::= or_expr (comp_operator or_expr)* comp_operator ::= "<" | ">" | "==" | ">=" | "<=" | "!=" | "is" ["not"] | ["not"] "in"

Operasi perbandingan menghasilkan nilai boolean: True atau False. Ekspresi dapat dirangkai secara berantai: contohnya x < y <= z ekuivalen dengan x < y and y <= z, di mana y hanya dievaluasi satu kali.
Perbandingan dapat dirangkai secara berantai: contohnya x < y <= z ekuivalen dengan x < y and y <= z, di mana y hanya dievaluasi satu kali saja.
Secara formal, jika a, b, c adalah ekspresi dan op1, op2 adalah operator perbandingan, maka a op1 b op2 c ekuivalen dengan a op1 b and b op2 c.
Perhatikan bahwa a op1 b op2 c tidak menyiratkan perbandingan langsung antara a dan c; sehingga ekspresi seperti x < y > z secara sintaksis valid di Python.
Perbandingan Nilai
Operator <, >, ==, >=, <=, dan != membandingkan nilai dari dua buah objek. Objek-objek tersebut tidak harus memiliki tipe data yang sama.
Bab Objek, nilai, dan tipe menyatakan bahwa setiap objek di Python memiliki nilai, tipe, dan identitas unik di memori.
Karena semua tipe adalah subtipe dari object, mereka mewarisi perilaku perbandingan default dari object.
Perilaku default perbandingan kesetaraan (== dan !=) didasarkan pada identitas objek di memori.
Perbandingan urutan default (<, >, <=, >=) tidak disediakan secara bawaan; mencobanya pada objek acak akan memicu TypeError.

The behavior of the default equality comparison, that instances with different
identities are always unequal, may be in contrast to what types will need that
have a sensible definition of object value and value-based equality.  Such
types will need to customize their comparison behavior, and in fact, a number
of built-in types have done that.

The following list describes the comparison behavior of the most important
built-in types.

items.html: Numbers of built-in numeric types (Numeric Types — int, float, complex) and of the standard library types fractions.Fraction and decimal.Decimal can be compared within and across their types, with the restriction that complex numbers do not support order comparison. Within the limits of the types involved, they compare mathematically (algorithmically) correct without loss of precision.

The not-a-number values float('NaN') and decimal.Decimal('NaN') are special. Any ordered comparison of a number to a not-a-number value is false. A counter-intuitive implication is that not-a-number values are not equal to themselves. For example, if x = float('NaN'), 3 < x, x < 3 and x == x are all false, while x != x is true. This behavior is compliant with IEEE 754.
None and NotImplemented are singletons. PEP 8 advises that comparisons for singletons should always be done with is or is not, never the equality operators.
Binary sequences (instances of bytes or bytearray) can be compared within and across their types. They compare lexicographically using the numeric values of their elements.
Strings (instances of str) compare lexicographically using the numerical Unicode code points (the result of the built-in function ord()) of their characters. [3]
Strings and binary sequences cannot be directly compared.

Sequences (instances of tuple, list, or range) can be compared only within each of their types, with the restriction that ranges do not support order comparison. Equality comparison across these types results in inequality, and ordering comparison across these types raises TypeError.

Sequences compare lexicographically using comparison of corresponding
elements.  The built-in containers typically assume identical objects are
equal to themselves.  That lets them bypass equality tests for identical
objects to improve performance and to maintain their internal invariants.
Lexicographical comparison between built-in collections works as follows:

For two collections to compare equal, they must be of the same type, have the same length, and each pair of corresponding elements must compare equal (for example, [1,2] == (1,2) is false because the type is not the same).

Collections that support order comparison are ordered the same as their first unequal elements (for example, [1,2,x] <= [1,2,y] has the same value as x <= y). If a corresponding element does not exist, the shorter collection is ordered first (for example, [1,2] < [1,2,3] is true).
Mappings (instances of dict) compare equal if and only if they have equal (key, value) pairs. Equality comparison of the keys and values enforces reflexivity.
Order comparisons (<, >, <=, and >=) raise TypeError.
Sets (instances of set or frozenset) can be compared within and across their types.

They define order comparison operators to mean subset and superset tests. Those relations do not define total orderings (for example, the two sets {1,2} and {2,3} are not equal, nor subsets of one another, nor supersets of one another). Accordingly, sets are not appropriate arguments for functions which depend on total ordering (for example, min(), max(), and sorted() produce undefined results given a list of sets as inputs).
Comparison of sets enforces reflexivity of its elements.

Most other built-in types have no comparison methods implemented, so they
inherit the default comparison behavior.

blocks.html:
User-defined classes that customize their comparison behavior should follow
some consistency rules, if possible:

items.html:
Equality comparison should be reflexive.
In other words, identical objects should compare equal:

blocks.html: x is y implies x == y

items.html:
Comparison should be symmetric.
In other words, the following expressions should have the same result:

blocks.html: x == y and y == x
x != y and y != x
x < y and y > x
x <= y and y >= x

items.html:
Comparison should be transitive.
The following (non-exhaustive) examples illustrate that:

blocks.html: x > y and y > z implies x > z
x < y and y <= z implies x < z

items.html:
Inverse comparison should result in the boolean negation.
In other words, the following expressions should have the same result:

blocks.html: x == y and not x != y
x < y and not x >= y (for total ordering)
x > y and not x <= y (for total ordering)

items.html: The last two expressions apply to totally ordered collections (e.g. to sequences, but not to sets or mappings). See also the total_ordering() decorator.
The hash() result should be consistent with equality. Objects that are equal should either have the same hash value, or be marked as unhashable.

blocks.html:
Python does not enforce these consistency rules. In fact, the not-a-number
values are an example for not following these rules.
Operasi Uji Keanggotaan (in, not in)
Operator in dan not in menguji keanggotaan suatu elemen di dalam sebuah koleksi (koleksi urutan seperti string, list, tuple, atau dictionary).
Untuk tipe string dan bytes, x in y bernilai True jika dan hanya jika x merupakan substring dari y. String kosong "" selalu dianggap sebagai substring dari string apa pun.
Untuk kelas kustom yang mendefinisikan metode __contains__(), ekspresi x in y bernilai True jika y.__contains__(x) mengembalikan nilai benar.

For user-defined classes which do not define __contains__() but do define __iter__(), x in y is True if some value z, for which the expression x is z or x == z is true, is produced while iterating over y. If an exception is raised during the iteration, it is as if in raised that exception.

Lastly, the old-style iteration protocol is tried: if a class defines __getitem__(), x in y is True if and only if there is a non-negative integer index i such that x is y[i] or x == y[i], and no lower integer index raises the IndexError exception. (If any other exception is raised, it is as if in raised that exception).
Operator not in didefinisikan memiliki nilai kebenaran terbalik dari operator in.
Perbandingan Identitas (is, is not)
Operator is dan is not menguji identitas objek: x is y bernilai benar jika dan hanya jika x dan y merupakan objek fisik yang sama persis di memori (memiliki nilai id() identik).
Operasi Boolean
or_test ::= and_test | or_test "or" and_test and_test ::= not_test | and_test "and" not_test not_test ::= comparison | "not" not_test
blocks.text:
or_test  ::= and_test | or_test "or" and_test
and_test ::= not_test | and_test "and" not_test
not_test ::= comparison | "not" not_test

blocks.html: In the context of Boolean operations, and also when expressions are used by control flow statements, the following values are interpreted as false: False, None, numeric zero of all types, and empty strings and containers (including strings, tuples, lists, dictionaries, sets and frozensets). All other values are interpreted as true. User-defined objects can customize their truth value by providing a __bool__() method.
Operator not menghasilkan True jika argumennya bernilai salah, dan sebaliknya menghasilkan False.
Ekspresi x and y pertama-tama mengevaluasi x; jika x bernilai salah, maka nilainya langsung dikembalikan; jika tidak, y dievaluasi dan hasilnya dikembalikan.
Ekspresi x or y pertama-tama mengevaluasi x; jika x bernilai benar, nilainya langsung dikembalikan; jika salah, maka y dievaluasi dan hasilnya dikembalikan.
Perhatikan bahwa baik and maupun or tidak membatasi nilai kembali pada True dan False literal, melainkan mengembalikan argumen terakhir yang dievaluasi.
Ekspresi Kondisional (Ternary)
conditional_expression ::= or_test ["if" or_test "else" expression] expression ::= conditional_expression | lambda_expr
blocks.text:
conditional_expression ::= or_test ["if" or_test "else" expression]
expression             ::= conditional_expression | lambda_expr

blocks.html: Ekspresi kondisional (sering disebut sebagai "operator ternary") memiliki bentuk x if C else y. Pertama-tama kondisi C dievaluasi; jika benar, nilai x dikembalikan; jika salah, nilai y yang dikembalikan.
Ekspresi x if C else y pertama-tama mengevaluasi kondisi C. Jika C bernilai benar, x dievaluasi dan nilainya dikembalikan; jika tidak, y dievaluasi dan nilainya dikembalikan.
See PEP 308 for more details about conditional expressions.
